transcript:
Meeting: Verdant - Escalation postmortem follow-up
Date/Time: 2027-04-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Sofia Rivera (Redwood CSM), Daniel Kim (Verdant CTO), Priya Shah (Verdant Head of ML Ops), Ethan Ross (Verdant SRE), Maya Lopez (Verdant Security)

Summary: quick sync to walk through root cause we tracked, confirm mitigations deployed, align on runbook updates and next steps for a short dedicated trial.
Topics: root cause breakdown, short-term mitigations, longer term reliability improvements, dedicated capacity pilot, security/audit questions

Transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: okay everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this to about 45, 50 minutes, quick follow-up from last week's incident and the postmortem draft we sent out. Liam will lead the tech side.
00:18 Liam Patel: hey, hi all, just to recap quickly, the outage was a cascade starting with a sudden traffic spike, combined with a suboptimal KV cache eviction under our prefix caching logic, and then a small networking blip on the VPC egress path. that caused long tail latencies, which pushed some upstream retries and then overloaded the request queue on a subset of dedicated hosts.
00:36 Daniel Kim: can you explain the cache thing again? we saw high CPU then a drop off, hard to correlate with our metrics.
00:48 Liam Patel: yeah so the runtime had an edge-case where when prefix cache miss rates jump from 5% to 60% in 2 minutes, the continuous batching logic backfills KVs and that suddenly increases memory pressure; in one cluster the process queued while GC ran then latency spiked. our mitigation is to add a fast-path that bypasses batch backfill if miss-rate delta > threshold, and to surface the KV eviction metric to the console so you can alert earlier.
01:12 Priya Shah: got it, and the networking blip — was that in Redwood's region or our cloud networking?
01:20 Liam Patel: preliminary show it's cloud VPC NAT gateway flaps, which led to a handful of connections failing and retries magnifying traffic. Redwood has a routing fallback we implemented mid-incident but the combination is what caused the cascade.
01:34 Ethan Ross: the retry storm was brutal on our end, our sidecar retrier also retried aggressively. we need a coordinated retry budget doc.
01:46 Sofia Rivera: already on it — we'll share a retrier guidance doc and a suggested retry-budget implementation.
01:52 Maya Lopez: on security/audit, we want confirmation that logs for the impacted timeframe were not redacted and are stored in the audit bucket, plus proof-of-delivery for that export.
02:04 Sofia Rivera: yes, we exported full request traces for the window and pushed to the bucket you provided; i'll share S3 paths in a separate email, and we'll include checksums.
02:12 Maya Chen: quick pause — are we okay with the proposed timeline in the draft postmortem (mitigations by 4/22, runbook updates by 4/26)?
02:22 Daniel Kim: timeline looks fine if we get the dedicated trial scheduled within two weeks.
02:29 Liam Patel: technical notes — short term patch is already staged, suppresses the batch backfill for the first minute after a miss-rate spike, which prevents the GC spike; medium-term is improved kernel-level memory accounting for quantized models and better prewarming.
02:46 Priya Shah: for model quantization — we run a mix of 7B and 13B; how confident are we that changes won't regress output quality?
02:56 Liam Patel: we'll run our eval harness on your prompt set, Sofia, against the quantized build; SE will share a report. quality gating is required before rolling to prod.
03:08 Daniel Kim: can we also get an A/B where some routes stay on hosted and some on dedicated to see delta in latency and cost?
03:16 Maya Chen: absolutely, that's our recommended canary. Liam can configure route-based rollout and Redwood's console shows token-level cost and latency by route.
03:26 Ethan Ross: what about SLA compensation talks — our VP of Eng asked about credits because this was a customer-facing degradation.
03:36 Maya Chen: we need to handle that via our CS/Legal process; Sofia will collect evidence and we'll route to the account team. any formal credit is contingent on contractual SLAs and the timeline agreed in the postmortem.
03:50 Sofia Rivera: noted, i'll pull the incident timeline and the alert hooks and open the case with ops.
03:57 Priya Shah: on the runbook, can you include steps for toggling dedicated burst capacity and a failover to hosted variants?
04:06 Liam Patel: yes, we have documented the exact commands for burst-enable and model-variant fallback; we'll add them to the Verdant runbook.
04:14 Daniel Kim: one more ask — are the KV cache and prefix keys exposed in the logs? our compliance team wants to ensure no PII is leaked.
04:24 Maya Lopez: yes, we require that no user PII is logged. please confirm the export is scrubbed or tokenized.
04:30 Sofia Rivera: confirmation: logs are key-hashed and we can provide a scrubbed sample.
04:36 Liam Patel: technical deep dive note — during the incident a subset of model kernels hit a regression in our scheduler that increased tail latency for seq-len 1024 by about 35% under contended GPUs; we've pinned those kernels and we'll push a micro-optimization to the runtime.
04:54 Daniel Kim: timeline?
05:00 Liam Patel: micro-opt in can roll out by 4/24 after our perf bench; we've scheduled a bench on your staging with your worst-case prompt set.
05:08 Priya Shah: how do we participate in the bench? we need run artifacts and an annotated spreadsheet for cost comparison.
05:15 Liam Patel: we'll run with the same input set you provide, output logs and per-token cost breakdown, and share a spreadsheet.
05:22 Maya Chen: action items recap in the chat but quick verbal recap: SE leads bench, Priya sends traffic/profile, Sofia sends contract/trial docs, Ethan verifies VPC flows, Redwood shares postmortem final.
05:40 Daniel Kim: thank you, appreciate the quick response and clear mitigations.
05:46 Maya Chen: thanks everyone we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mislabels (some speaker overlap around 02:00). There are references to internal kernels and KV cache that may be slightly abbreviated due to auto-transcription.

References shared: Postmortem draft (link: https://redwood.company/postmortems/VA-20270414), Runbook stub (link: https://redwood.company/runbooks/verdant-kv-eviction), Benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared by SE), Audit export S3 path (provided separately).

End of transcript.
